blocks.text: Tranebær bedømmes på farve, glans og ensartethed. Stød, sen høst og dårlig udluftning giver bløde, gummiagtige bær.

sourceRef.locator: Cranberry chapter, Quality Characteristics and Criteria; Physiological Disorders, pp. 297–299
sourceRef.quote: Color intensity, glossiness, uniformity, and freedom from defects are the major quality characteristics for fresh and frozen cranberries … Physiological breakdown of cranberry is manifested by a soft and rubbery condition, dull external appearance, and diffusion of red anthocyanin pigment throughout internal tissues … It is correlated with one or more of the following: impact bruising; late-harvested, more intensely colored fruit;

sourceRef.locator: Cranberry chapter, Optimum Storage Conditions, p. 297
sourceRef.quote: The minimum recommended storage temperature is 2 °C (35.6 °F). The maximum recommended temperature is 4 to 5 °C (39 to 41 °F) … The recommended RH is 90 to 95%

blocks.text: Tranebær er kuldefølsomme: Over ca. 4 uger nær 0 °C kan de blive matte og gummiagtige og rådne lettere.

sourceRef.quote: Cranberry is considered to be a chilling sensitive fruit … Storage at temperatures near 0 °C for more than about 4 weeks may result in low- temperature breakdown (Lidster et al. 1988). Chilling injury symptoms include dull appearance, rubbery texture, and increased decay

blocks.text: Tranebær danner lidt ethylen (en gas, som frugt og grønt selv afgiver, og som får dem til at modne).

sourceRef.locator: Cranberry chapter, Ethylene Production and Sensitivity, p. 298
sourceRef.quote: Cranberry has a low ethylene production rate of 0.1 to 1.0 μL kg-1 h-1 at 5 °C (41 °F)

blocks.text: Friske tranebær kan holde 2–4 måneder, afhængigt af sæson, sort, modenhed og håndtering. Tidligt høstede bær holder normalt længere end sent høstede.

sourceRef.quote: Cranberries can be stored fresh for 2 to 4 mo, depending on season, cultivar, maturity, handling, and storage conditions (Hardenburg et al. 1986). … Early-harvested fruit usually have a longer storage potential than late-harvested fruit

blocks.text: Bær: Vælg faste, modne bær, vask dem godt, og lad dem være hele eller halver dem. Bær med fast skind dyppes 30 sekunder i kogende vand, så skindet revner. Bløde bær (jordbær) lægges 10 minutter i vand med C-vitamin (ascorbinsyre). Lad dem dryppe godt af, og læg dem højst to lag dybt. Tør dem, til de er hårde og rasler, når bakken rystes (24–36 timer).

sourceRef.quote: Berries Select firm ripe fruit. Wash well. Leave whole or cut in half. For berries with firm skins, dip in boiling water 30 seconds to crack skins. For berries with soft skins (strawberries), dip in ascorbic acid or other antimicrobial solution for 10 minutes. Remove and drain well. Place on drying trays not more than two berries deep. Dry until hard and berries rattle when shaken on trays (24-36 hours).

blocks.text: Tør frugten i ét lag ved 60 °C i ovnen eller i et tørreapparat. Vend store stykker hver 3.–4. time. Frugten er tør, når den er sej og kan bøjes. Test det: Lad et par stykker køle af, og klem en håndfuld. Hånden skal være tør, og stykkerne skal falde fra hinanden, når du slipper.

sourceRef.quote: Arrange pretreated fruits on drying trays in single layers, pit cavity up. Dry at 140 degrees F (60°C) in an oven or dehydrator. … If possible, stir food and turn large pieces over every 3 to 4 hours during the drying period. … Dried fruits should be leathery and pliable. … Squeeze a handful of the fruit. If no moisture is left on the hand and pieces spring apart when released, they are dry.

blocks.text: Lad frugten hvile i 4–10 dage i en beholder med et løst låg, og ryst den hver dag. Så fordeles den sidste fugt. Kommer der små dråber på indersiden, skal frugten tørre mere. Opbevar den derefter i en tæt beholder, køligt, tørt og mørkt. Så holder den 6–12 måneder.

sourceRef.quote: Lightly cover and store in a warm, dry, well-ventilated place for four to 10 days. Stir or shake containers daily to separate pieces. If beads of moisture form inside, return food to drying trays for further drying, then repeat the conditioning step. … Store in a cool, dry, dark place or in the refrigerator or freezer. Properly stored, dried fruits keep well for six to 12 months.

blocks.text: Uden strøm kan du tørre frugt ude i solen. Det kan lade sig gøre, fordi frugt har meget sukker og syre. Det tager flere dage og kræver varmt, tørt vejr med vind: mindst 29 °C og helst ikke for fugtig luft (under 60 % luftfugtighed). Dæk frugten til, eller tag den ind om natten, så den ikke bliver fugtig igen.

sourceRef.quote: The high sugar and acid content of fruits make them safe to dry out-of-doors when conditions are favorable for drying. … To dry fruits out-of-doors hot, dry, breezy days are best. A minimum temperature of 85ºF is needed with higher temperatures being better. It takes several days to dry foods out-of-doors. … A humidity below 60 percent is best. … Fruits dried out-of-doors must be covered or brought under shelter at night. The cool night air condenses and could add moisture back to the food, thus slowing down the drying process.

blocks.text: Tranebær-appelsin-chutney: ca. 680 g (24 oz) tranebær, løg, rosiner, sukker, eddike (5 %), appelsinsaft, ingefær og kanel simres ca. 15 minutter, fyldes varm på halv-pint-glas (ca. 2,5 dl) med 1,3 cm fri plads og henkoges 10 minutter i vandbad.

sourceRef.quote: 24 ounces fresh whole cranberries 2 cups chopped white onion 2 cups golden raisins 1½ cups white sugar 1½ cups packed brown sugar 2 cups white distilled vinegar (5%) 1 cup orange juice 4 teaspoons peeled, grated fresh ginger 3 sticks cinnamon … simmer gently for 15 minutes or until cranberries are tender. … Fill the hot chutney into clean, hot half-pint jars, leaving ½-inch headspace. … Hot Half-pints 10 min

blocks.text: Tranebærsauce: 4 cups tranebær koges møre i 1 cup vand, presses gennem en fin sigte, tilsættes 2 cups sukker og koger 3 minutter. Fyld den kogende sauce på varme glas med 1,3 cm fri plads, og henkog 15 minutter i vandbad (halv-pint- eller pint-glas, op til 300 m over havet).

sourceRef.quote: 4 cups cranberries 1 cup water 2 cups sugar … Cook berries in water until soft. Press through a fine sieve. Add sugar and boil 3 minutes. Pour boiling hot sauce into hot jars, leaving ½-inch headspace. … Hot Half-pints or Pints 15 min
